class.name: PhysXLensFlareSettings
class.brief_description: How a [PhysXLensFlare3D] looks, provided by the PhysX module.
class.description: A [PhysXLensFlare3D]'s look, as a resource, so it can be saved as a preset and shared between scenes. The defaults are a warm, eight-ghost camera flare. Each ghost is a copy of the frame's bright light reflected about the screen's centre, given by a color in [member ghost_colors] and a scale at the same index in [member ghost_scales]. A light at some distance from the centre shows up at that distance divided by the scale, drawn [code]1 / |scale|[/code] times its size: [code]-1[/code] mirrors it through the centre at its own size, [code]2[/code] draws it half as large, halfway to the centre on the same side, [code]-0.5[/code] twice as large and twice as far out on the opposite side (a ghost drawn larger spreads the same light thinner, so it's dimmer). Up to 8 ghosts.

members.member: The colored fringe on each ghost: its red, green and blue are drawn slightly apart, by this fraction of the ghost's distance from the screen's centre. Around [code]0.01[/code]-[code]0.03[/code] gives the thin fringe of a real lens; much larger pulls the ghosts apart into separate red, green and blue copies. [code]0[/code] for none; negative swaps red and blue.

Each ghost's color; its alpha scales that ghost's brightness (alpha [code]0[/code] hides it). Entry [i]n[/i] here and entry [i]n[/i] of [member ghost_scales] make ghost [i]n[/i]: only as many ghosts are drawn as both arrays have entries, 8 at most. Add or remove an entry in both to add or remove a ghost.
How bright all the ghosts are. Set it to [code]0[/code] to tune the halo on its own.

Where each ghost sits and how big it is; entry [i]n[/i] pairs with entry [i]n[/i] of [member ghost_colors]. Ghosts line up along the line from the light through the screen's centre: - [b]Negative[/b]: on the opposite side of the centre from the light ([code]-1[/code] is the exact mirror point, at the light's own size). - [b]Positive[/b]: on the light's own side, between it and the centre. - [b]Large[/b] ([code]5[/code], [code]10[/code]): small and close to the centre. - [b]Near 0[/b] ([code]-0.2[/code], [code]0.7[/code]): large, soft and faint, far out along the line (a ghost drawn larger spreads the same light thinner). A ghost is drawn [code]1 / |scale|[/code] times the light's size, at its distance from the centre divided by the scale.
The halo's rainbow edge: how far apart its red, green and blue rings are drawn. Small values give a thin colored rim; larger ones a broad rainbow band. Negative reverses the order of the colors.
Bends the screen like a fisheye before the ring is drawn, so the ring stays round and closer to the light near the screen's edges. [code]0[/code] for a plain ring.

How bright the halo is. The halo is a ring around the screen's centre that a bright light lights up as an arc on the far side of the ring; it moves as the light moves. Set [member ghost_intensity] to [code]0[/code] to see it on its own.
How much of the ring toward the screen's centre is faded out: at [code]0.5[/code] it fades in from the centre to the screen's edge; nearer [code]1[/code] only the outermost part shows.
The ring's diameter, as a fraction of the screen's height.
How bright the whole flare is. [code]0[/code] draws nothing.

How bright (linear HDR luminance) a part of the frame must be before it flares. Every bright part flares, not only lights: a sunlit surface or the glow around the sun makes its own ghosts too. Raise this to keep the flare to the real light sources; lower it for more glow. In Godot's default scenes the sky is around [code]0.5[/code] and the sun's disk around [code]2[/code], so the useful range is narrow.
How far above [member threshold] a light must be to flare fully; it eases in over this range, so lights crossing the threshold don't pop.
